title: Humanity and Incarnation of Christ
definition: The humanity and incarnation of Christ is the doctrine that the eternal Son of God truly became man without ceasing to be God.
summary: Jesus Christ is fully God and fully man, entering human life to redeem sinners.
christFocus: In the incarnation, Jesus came near to sinners, took on true humanity, and became the mediator who represents His people before God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The incarnation means the eternal Son of God took on real human nature. Jesus was not pretending to be human, nor was He merely appearing in human form. He was born, grew, became tired, experienced hunger, suffered, wept, obeyed, and died.

At the same time, Jesus never stopped being God. The mystery of the incarnation is that the one Person, Jesus Christ, is truly God and truly man. He enters the human condition without sin in order to redeem those under sin.

Because Christ became truly human, He can represent His people. Because He is truly God, He can save completely. His incarnation reveals both the humility of the Son and the mercy of God toward broken humanity.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People who suffer often wonder whether God is distant from human weakness. The incarnation shows that the Son of God entered real human life and knows suffering from within. He is not detached from weakness; He came near to redeem and help.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your weakness, suffering, and need to Christ with confidence. Follow His humility, marvel at His nearness, and remember that your Savior is both fully able to save and fully able to sympathize.
